labels.date_clause_none: No clear reply date is given. Treat 15 days from receipt as your working deadline.
labels.disclaimer: NyayaDost explains documents in plain language. It is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. Verify important steps with a licensed advocate or your District Legal Services Authority.
labels.reply_note: This is a starting draft, not legal advice. Fill in the blanks and have it checked before sending. Keep the postal receipt and proof of delivery.

common_steps.title: Reply in writing before the deadline
common_steps.detail: Send a clear, polite written reply. Keep a copy for yourself and proof that you sent it.

common_steps.title: Use registered post or speed post
common_steps.detail: Do not rely only on WhatsApp or a phone call for a formal notice. Keep the postal receipt and tracking number.

common_steps.title: Gather your documents
common_steps.detail: Attach copies, never originals, of the agreement, receipts, cheque, bank memo, or payment proof.

common_steps.title: Do not ignore the notice or sign under pressure
common_steps.detail: Ignoring a notice can lead to a case. Do not sign blank papers or agree to a payment you do not owe.

common_steps.title: Get free legal help if you need it
common_steps.detail: Call the NALSA helpline at 15100 or contact your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA).

summary_frame: This notice is about {topic}. According to {sender}, {allegation}. {date_clause} If you do not respond, {consequence}.

legal_notice.meaning: A formal written warning sent before starting a legal case.

statutory_notice.meaning: A notice that a law requires a person to send within a fixed time.

cheque_dishonour.meaning: When a bank refuses to pay a cheque, for example because the account has insufficient funds.

demand_notice.meaning: A formal notice asking for money or for a specific action.

registered_post.meaning: A postal service that gives written proof of delivery.

affidavit.meaning: A written statement sworn on oath, usually used as evidence.

injunction.meaning: A court order that stops a person from doing something or requires them to do it.

limitation_period.meaning: The legal time limit for filing a case or appeal.

tenancy.meaning: The legal relationship created when a person occupies property for rent.

maintenance.meaning: Money paid for the financial support of a family member.

sarfaesi.meaning: A law that lets a secured lender enforce security without going to court first, subject to strict rules.

arbitration.meaning: A dispute resolution process decided by a neutral arbitrator outside court.

consumer_protection.meaning: Laws that protect buyers of goods and services from defects and unfair practices.

e_daakhil.meaning: The official portal for filing consumer complaints online.

title_deed.meaning: A legal document that shows ownership of property.

assessment.meaning: The tax department's process of checking your income and deciding the tax due.

cheque_bounce.label: Cheque Bounce Notice
cheque_bounce.topic: a cheque that your bank returned unpaid
cheque_bounce.allegation: a cheque you issued was dishonoured by the bank, and the amount remains unpaid
cheque_bounce.consequence: the complainant may file a criminal complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
cheque_bounce.deadline_label: Pay the cheque amount or send a written reply
cheque_bounce.secondary_label: The complainant's criminal complaint window closes around this date
cheque_bounce.extra_step_detail: Ask your bank for the cheque return memo. Confirm the reason (insufficient funds, stop payment, signature mismatch) and the date the cheque was returned.

rent_eviction.label: Rent / Eviction Notice
rent_eviction.statute: State rent control law and Transfer of Property Act, 1882
rent_eviction.topic: your tenancy and a demand to vacate the premises
rent_eviction.allegation: you have defaulted on rent or are being asked to vacate the rented premises
rent_eviction.consequence: the landlord may file an eviction suit or a recovery case before the civil court
rent_eviction.deadline_label: Reply to the landlord or vacate as demanded
rent_eviction.extra_step_title: Check your rent agreement and payment receipts
rent_eviction.extra_step_detail: Compare the notice period with your rent agreement and your state's rent law. Keep bank statements, rent receipts, and messages about payments.

loan_recovery.label: Loan Recovery Notice
loan_recovery.statute: RBI recovery norms, SARFAESI Act, 2002, and civil law
loan_recovery.allegation: a loan amount or EMI is overdue and the lender is demanding payment
loan_recovery.consequence: the lender may start recovery action, arbitration, or a civil suit, and a secured loan may face action under SARFAESI
loan_recovery.extra_step_title: Ask for a full statement of account
loan_recovery.extra_step_detail: Request a written statement showing the principal, interest, penalties, and payments already made. Check whether the recovery agent is authorised by the lender.

consumer.label: Consumer Complaint Notice
consumer.topic: a defective product or a deficient service
consumer.allegation: a product or service you paid for was defective or deficient, and the seller or provider has not resolved it
consumer.consequence: the consumer may file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
consumer.extra_step_title: Collect your invoice, warranty, and complaint records
consumer.extra_step_detail: Keep the bill, warranty card, product photos or videos, service tickets, and every email or chat where you raised the complaint.

maintenance.label: Maintenance / Family Notice
maintenance.statute: Section 144, BNSS, 2023 and applicable family law
maintenance.topic: maintenance or financial support for a family member
maintenance.allegation: you have not paid maintenance or support that the sender says is legally due
maintenance.consequence: the sender may file a maintenance case under Section 144 of the BNSS, 2023 or the applicable family law
maintenance.extra_step_title: Gather income, expense, and family records
maintenance.extra_step_detail: Keep salary slips, bank statements, rent and school fee receipts, and any earlier court order. Do not stop responding just because the relationship has broken down.

property.label: Property / Possession Notice
property.statute: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and Specific Relief Act, 1963
property.topic: ownership, possession, or a boundary dispute over property
property.allegation: you are occupying, encroaching on, or interfering with property that the sender claims
property.consequence: the sender may file a civil suit for possession, injunction, or declaration
property.extra_step_title: Verify the title chain and survey records
property.extra_step_detail: Collect the sale deed, mutation entries, property tax receipts, survey map, and photographs. Do not sign any document or give possession without written advice.

employment.label: Employment / Salary Notice
employment.statute: Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 and state labour law
employment.topic: unpaid salary, termination, or another employment dispute
employment.allegation: your employer or employee has not met a salary, notice-period, or termination obligation
employment.consequence: the other side may approach the labour commissioner or an industrial tribunal
employment.extra_step_title: Build a dated record of your employment
employment.extra_step_detail: Keep the appointment letter, salary slips, attendance records, emails, and the termination or resignation letter. Note every unpaid amount and date.

tax.label: Tax Department Notice
tax.topic: an income tax or GST notice
tax.allegation: the tax department has raised a discrepancy, demand, or query about your return
tax.consequence: the department may complete the assessment, impose interest or penalty, or reopen the case
tax.extra_step_title: Log in to the official tax portal
tax.extra_step_detail: Open the e-filing portal and read the notice and its annexures. Check the assessment year, section, and response deadline. Never pay a demand without verifying it on the official portal.

generic.label: Legal Notice
generic.allegation: the sender says you owe money, must act, or must stop doing something
generic.consequence: the sender may file a case or start other legal action
generic.extra_step_title: Identify the sender and the exact demand
generic.extra_step_detail: Read the notice twice. Write down who sent it, what they want, the date, the amount, and the documents they mention. Do not reply only by phone.
